(`AppMenuRow.ordered` and `.title`; the last row's title is
This file is the machine-readable twin the web renders from, so the browser app and the
phone name the same doors in the same order. Both sides are pinned by
web/tools/verify_app_shell.py: it reads the three Swift files above and this JSON and
fails when they disagree, and it reads web/app/index.html and fails when the page has
drifted from the JSON. Change the Swift first, then this file.
`waysIn` is the web's half of the empty Sessions tab, and only the half the phone has
no words for. THE ROW ORDER AND THE ROW TITLES COME FROM docs/guide/getting-started.json
(pattern J in docs/review-checklist.md: the ways in have one order everywhere), so only
the `line` is authored here. `here` says whether a browser can open that door at all. A
row that says no says why in its own line, and still links to the route on /start/.
The two rows the phone does not have are `drop` and `example`. They are the analyzer's
own strengths, they lead the card, and they carry their own titles.
